newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to raise power tariffs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to raise power tariffs - paper.

text.p: Bangladesh, under pressure from international donors, has decided to raise electricity tariffs by 15 percent in stages from next month, the Janakantha newspaper reported.
The newspaper said the government had made the decision in a bid to cut losses incurred by the power generation system.
Farmers using electricity for running irrigation pumps would be exempted from the rise, the paper said.
The minimum electricity rate is currently 4.23 U.S. cents a kilowatt hour which officials say does not cover generating costs. The rates were last increased in in 1991.

The paper, quoting officials, said rising gas prices, inflation and currency depreciation had made the increase necessary. It said that over the past five years, gas prices had risen by 22 percent, inflation was up 19 percent and the taka had depreciated by 23 percent against the dollar.
More than 80 percent of Banagladesh's power plants are fuelled by natural gas. The country's gas reserves have been estimated at about 12 trillion cubic feet.
The Asian Development Bank recently warned Bangladesh that it would withdraw from funding a $300 million power project unless power tariffs were raised by 25 percent.
